Use Cases / Ideas: AI Exploratory Testing — E2E Flow Testing with Local LLMs
Description:
Rather than testing parts of a flow in isolation (unit tests), this workflow tests entire verticals end-to-end — like fuzzing. Feed the full source code of a Django backend (settings, middleware, views, URL config) to a local LLM. The AI traces through the complete request lifecycle — rate limiter → auth → RBAC → view → response — and generates adversarial curl commands that probe the full middleware chain. You run them against the live app (TDD approach: test and capture actual behavior), feed the results back, and the AI produces a structured bug report with flow traces, severity ratings, and fix suggestions. Demo: AI traces through a Django app's middleware stack and catches 7 real issues — rate limiter using wrong rejection policy, auth middleware not validating API keys on internal endpoints, RBAC using OR instead of AND for permission checks, path-matching bypass patterns, and IP spoofing in rate limiting. All passing happy-path tests, all invisible to unit tests.
Constraints:
1. Requires 16B+ parameter models for quality: E2E flow analysis across multiple files (settings, middleware, views) needs strong reasoning. 7B models may miss cross-file interactions. Recommend deepseek-coder-v2:16b or qwen2.5-coder:32b.
2. Behavioral testing — requires a running app: Unlike static analysis, the API must be running for you to execute curls and capture real responses. The TDD approach is: generate scenarios → run them → capture actual output → feed back to AI.
3. Not a substitute for security audits: AI catches common middleware flaws (auth bypass, rate limiter gaps) but is not a replacement for professional penetration testing or OWASP compliance.
4. LLM agnostic: The prompts work with any LLM — Ollama (local), ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or any other provider. No vendor lock-in. Ollama is recommended for data privacy but not required.
Tools Used:
Any LLM: The prompts are LLM-agnostic. Works with Ollama (local/free), ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or any coding-capable model. No vendor lock-in.

Flow (Optional):
Step 1: Start the sample Django API. Run: python manage.py runserver 8000. Verify with a happy-path test: curl http://localhost:8000/api/health — should return 200 OK. The app works. Unit tests would pass. But the middleware chain has 7 hidden E2E flow issues.
Step 2: Feed the full codebase to the LLM. Open Prompt 1 (prompts/01-generate-scenarios.md). Copy the prompt into your LLM of choice. Then paste the contents of all 7 source files — settings.py, urls.py, the 3 middleware files, api/urls.py, and api/views.py. The AI reads the full codebase, traces through the middleware chain, and generates 15 E2E test scenarios with exact curl commands. Each scenario includes a flow trace showing which middleware runs, what it checks, and where the AI predicts the flow will break.
Step 3: Run the curl commands against the live API (TDD approach). Execute each curl command against http://localhost:8000. This is Test-Driven — you do not assume behavior, you test and capture actual responses. Save each curl + response into test_results.txt. For the demo, run at least 8-10 scenarios covering: rate limiter bypass (POST requests skip it), auth bypass (any API key accepted on internal endpoints), RBAC bypass (user with one permission passes AND-required checks), path matching bypass (/api/products-admin skips auth).
Step 4: Feed results back to the AI for analysis. Open Prompt 2 (prompts/02-analyze-results.md). Copy the prompt into your LLM. Paste the contents of test_results.txt. The AI analyzes each response by tracing through the middleware chain and produces a structured bug report: severity, component, flow trace, impact, fix suggestion, and backwards compatibility notes.
Step 5: Review the AI bug report. The AI should identify 7 issues across the middleware stack: (1) rate limiter returns 200 instead of 429 — wrong rejection policy, (2) rate limiter only applies to GET — POST/PUT/DELETE bypass entirely, (3) rate limiter trusts X-Forwarded-For blindly — IP spoofing bypass, (4) internal endpoints check API key presence but not value, (5) RBAC uses OR instead of AND for permission checks, (6) public path matching uses startswith — /api/products-admin bypasses auth, (7) no token expiry validation.
Step 6: Fix the critical issues. Apply fixes to the middleware files — correct the rate limiter status code and method coverage, validate the actual API key value, change RBAC to use AND logic, use exact path matching. Re-run the failing scenarios to verify correct behavior.
Step 7: Verify the full flow end-to-end. Re-run all scenarios from Step 3. Confirm rate limiter returns 429, internal endpoints reject invalid keys, RBAC enforces all required permissions, and path manipulation no longer bypasses auth. The middleware chain is now production-ready.

Wow Factor / Hack:
Step 2 — AI Traces the Full Middleware Chain and Predicts Where It Breaks: The AI doesn't test endpoints in isolation — it reads the ENTIRE codebase (settings, middleware, views, URL config) and traces the full request lifecycle. It generates scenarios that probe cross-cutting concerns: does the rate limiter apply before or after auth? Does RBAC check all required permissions or just one? Can path manipulation skip middleware entirely? This is E2E flow testing — the kind that only a senior engineer who understands the full stack would do manually.
Step 4 — TDD Approach Validates AI Predictions Against Real Behavior: The AI generates scenarios and predicts failures. You run the curls against the live app and capture actual responses. Then you feed the real output back to the AI for analysis. This is Test-Driven Development applied to exploratory testing — you never assume behavior, you verify it. The AI's predictions matched reality in 7 out of 7 cases.
LLM Agnostic — No Vendor Lock-In: The two prompt templates work with ANY LLM — Ollama locally, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or any coding-capable model. No API-specific code, no vendor dependency. Viewers choose their preferred model and interface. Ollama is recommended for data privacy but the prompts are portable.
Reduces Manual Regression Testing Between Releases: The generated scenarios and prompts are reusable across releases. Before each deployment, re-run the same E2E flow tests to verify the middleware chain still works correctly. This reduces the manual regression testing burden and helps ensure backwards compatibility — the AI even flags which fixes could break existing clients.
Fully Local Option — Zero Data Privacy Risk: When used with Ollama, source code and test results never leave your machine. For backends handling sensitive data, this is the safest approach to AI-assisted testing.
Benefits:
- Tests entire verticals end-to-end instead of just units — catches middleware-level issues (auth bypass, rate limiter gaps, RBAC flaws) that unit tests are structurally blind to
- Reduced testing time — AI generates 15 targeted E2E scenarios in under a minute, covering flows that would take a manual QA engineer hours
- Faster releases — reusable prompts and scenarios can be re-run before every deployment as a regression check
- Fewer bugs that can't be caught with unit tests — the AI traces through the full middleware chain and finds cross-cutting issues
- Proves business logic is intact — verifies the full request flow (auth → RBAC → view) matches the design specification, not just individual function correctness
- LLM agnostic — prompts work with any model (Ollama, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini). No vendor lock-in, no API-specific code
- Helps ensure backwards compatibility — AI flags which fixes could affect existing consumers, reducing regression risk between releases
- When used with Ollama: zero cost, zero API keys, source code never leaves your machine
